title: How Netanyahu could attack Iran to force Israel into unity government after elections
gist: Political sources tell Al-Monitor a pre-election Israeli strike on Iran is off the table, but Netanyahu could attack right after the Oct. 27 vote to pressure rivals into a wartime unity government; Trump and IDF chief Zamir oppose renewed fighting.

insights.claim: Netanyahu could strike Iran immediately after the Oct. 27 Israeli election to pressure rivals into joining a wartime unity government, political sources told Al-Monitor.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Tail risk of renewed Israel-Iran fighting right after the vote; hedge oil and regional risk around Oct. 27-28.

insights.claim: A pre-election strike appears off the table, though sources say it cannot be entirely ruled out until election day.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Near-term strike probability is low but non-zero.
insights.locator: Tensions in Israel are running high

insights.claim: Trump opposes reigniting the conflict before the Nov. 3 US midterms; the FT, citing three diplomatic sources, reported Netanyahu had planned to strike Iran earlier in October.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: US domestic politics constrains Israeli action until after Nov. 3.

insights.claim: Trump sent Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to Israel on an unannounced visit; Reuters cited three Israeli officials saying they discussed the Iranian file.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit

insights.claim: IDF chief Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir has signaled little appetite for more fighting and held conversations with US counterparts in early October on the implications for Israel's elections.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.so_what: Military leadership is a brake on a political-timing strike.

insights.claim: Netanyahu appears to have failed in recent attempts to reignite hostilities with Iran as a way to delay what could be the most consequential election of his career.
insights.speaker: Ben Caspit
insights.locator: As Al-Monitor has reported on Tuesday
